title.narrative: Policies & programmes to promote full, productive & decent employment opertationalised

description.narrative: Bangladesh faces challenges in quality employment amid ongoing structural transformation. While employment in industry and services has grown, reliance on the ready-made garment (RMG) sector remains high, with limited diversification. Agriculture’s declining contribution to poverty reduction, sluggish private investment, and informal, low-productivity jobs further constrain inclusive growth. Youth unemployment, at 12.8%, and over 12 million youth not in employment, education, or training (NEET), underscore an urgent need for targeted skills development and job creation. Women face significant disadvantages, reflected in lower labour force participation, high levels of unpaid work, and underrepresentation in formal employment. The ILO’s strategy emphasizes more and better-quality jobs by strengthening employment policies and skills systems. Strategies include rolling out the costed National Action Plan for the updated National Employment Policy 2022, promoting robust skills and lifelong learning systems with a focus on advanced, digital, and gender-responsive skills, and operationalizing the Bangladesh National Qualifications Framework (BNQF). The ILO will also work on digitalized skills needs assessment and forecasting systems and expand private sector-led apprenticeships, workplace learning, and employment support services. Expected results include enhanced employability for young people and women, improved access to quality jobs, strengthened skills systems, and greater alignment between skills supply and labour market demand. Beneficiaries are primarily youth, women, returnee migrants, indigenous groups, persons with disabilities. Partners include government bodies such as the Ministry of Education, National Skills Development Authority, Ministry of Labour and Employment, Ministry of Expatriate Welfare and Overseas Employment, Ministry of Youth and Sports, and employers’ organizations, chambers of commerce, industry associations, and development partners.
